# ezghcloud_kubernetes_cluster (Resource)

An EZGH Kubernetes cluster: a Kubernetes control plane EZGH runs, reached at one endpoint, in your VPC. Its nodes come from ezghcloud_kubernetes_node_group. A cluster with node groups can't be destroyed: destroy them first.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `bot_id` (String) Cluster Bot (bot_): load balancers, volumes and node capacity the cluster makes are made as this Bot. Needs KubernetesClusterAccess, and the caller needs bots.pass on it. It can't change after create: replacing a cluster would lose its workloads, so a change is refused at plan.
- `name` (String) Cluster name. Changing it replaces the cluster.
- `project_id` (String) Project identifier. Changing it replaces the cluster.
- `subnet_id` (String) Subnet (sbn_) the endpoint's private addresses live in. Its route table must send 0.0.0.0/0 to a Network Gateway. It can't change after create: replacing a cluster would lose its workloads, so a change is refused at plan.

### Optional

- `bootstrap_creator_access` (Boolean) Give the caller who creates the cluster an access entry with cluster admin. It can't change after create: replacing a cluster would lose its workloads, so a change is refused at plan.
- `encryption_key_id` (String) Keys key (kms_) Kubernetes Secrets are encrypted with. Left out, an EZGH-managed key. It can't change after create: replacing a cluster would lose its workloads, so a change is refused at plan.
- `logging_project_id` (String) Project (prj_) whose Obs receives the control-plane logs. Required with logging_types.
- `logging_types` (Set of String) Control-plane logs sent to logging_project_id's Obs: api, audit, authenticator, controllerManager and scheduler. Billed as log ingest.
- `maintenance_window_day` (String) Day of the weekly 4-hour maintenance window, monday to sunday. Set with maintenance_window_start_hour; left out at create, EZGH picks one; removed later, the last window stays.
- `maintenance_window_start_hour` (Number) Start hour (UTC, 0 to 23) of the maintenance window.
- `operation_timeout` (String) Maximum wait for each asynchronous operation, for example 45m.
- `public_access_cidrs` (List of String) IPv4 CIDRs allowed to reach the public endpoint, at most 40. Left out at create, 0.0.0.0/0; removed later, the last value stays. An empty list closes the public endpoint: kubectl then reaches the cluster only from inside the VPC.
- `service_ipv4_cidr` (String) IPv4 range Services get addresses from. Left out, 10.100.0.0/16. It can't change after create: replacing a cluster would lose its workloads, so a change is refused at plan.
- `tags` (Map of String) Resource tags.
- `version` (String) Kubernetes minor version, such as 1.37. Left out, the newest offered. Upgrades in place one minor version at a time; a downgrade is refused at plan. Node groups keep their version until each is upgraded.

### Read-Only

- `certificate_authority` (String) The cluster CA certificate, PEM; null until the cluster is active.
- `endpoint_hostname` (String) The endpoint's public DNS name, for kubectl.
- `endpoint_private_hostname` (String) The endpoint's DNS name inside the VPC.
- `endpoint_public_ipv4` (String) The endpoint's public IPv4 address; null until assigned.
- `id` (String) Cluster ID (kcl_).
- `node_firewall_id` (String) Firewall (fwl_) the cluster's nodes are in.
- `oidc_issuer` (String) The cluster's service account token issuer, for other OIDC relying parties.
- `operation_id` (String) Most recent operation initiated by this resource; unavailable on import.
- `organization_id` (String) Organization managed by the configured provider.
- `patch_version` (String) The patch release the control plane runs; EZGH updates it in the weekly maintenance window.
- `resource_name` (String) IAM resource name.
- `service_ipv6_cidr` (String) IPv6 range Services get addresses from.
- `status` (String) What the cluster is doing: creating, active, updating, deleting or failed.
- `vpc_id` (String) VPC of the subnet.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Replace identifiers with values from your organization.
terraform import ezghcloud_kubernetes_cluster.example 'ORGANIZATION_ID/PROJECT_ID/CLUSTER_ID'
```
